terms.gloss: mutter, murmur, speak under one’s breath
evidence: Liv. 33.31: clam mussantēs (Lewis & Short; not in Cicero or Caesar)
terms.comment: Varro derives it from the sound mū, the least a mute man can say (L.L. 7.101): rightly, an imitative word. Lewis & Short notes that it is not used by Cicero or Caesar.

evidence: Plaut. Mil. 3.1.149: servī murmurant, of grumbling (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Nimis crūdum est hoc pōmum. — Quid tū mussās?
phrases.english: This apple is too green. — What are you muttering?

sources: Lewis & Short: musso · Lewis & Short: murmuro
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 349.
Vives quoted from the Latinitas loci collection, checked against a single transcription; a modern school dialogue, not a classical source.
